description: The gradient of a convolution with respect to its filter: dw from x and dy. The same problem space as conv_fwd -- dy has y's shape and dw has w's.

groups.description: Convolution groups. Not a schema field: the frontend derives it as xDims[1] / wDims[1], so it is said by giving the filter C/groups input channels. groups == C is a depthwise convolution.

dtype.description: Element type of x, w and y. The list is the subset of the backend's eighteen convertible types that a convolution is actually run in: the float types, the fp8 pairs including the FNUZ spellings AMD hardware uses, and int8 for quantized inference. Types reached only through block scaling (fp4, fp6, int4) are declared on the quantize operations that produce them, not here.

spatial.description: 2-D ([N, C, H, W]) or 3-D ([N, C, D, H, W]) convolution.

D.description: Input depth; 1 and absent from the tensors for 2-D.

layout.description: NCHW/NCDHW (filter KCRS) or NHWC/NDHWC (filter KRSC) memory order.

graph_builder.// types: Operands carry the declared dtype; accumulation is fp32 regardless. That is what mixed precision means -- fp16 or bf16 storage with fp32 accumulate -- and it is also a hard gate: MIOpen's convolution builder declines any node whose compute_data_type is not FLOAT, so a uniform-fp16 graph is refused before applicability is even considered.

archetypes.name: valid_3x3
archetypes.note: VALID padding: the output shrinks by R-1 rather than holding the extent

archetypes.name: valid_1x1_stride4
archetypes.note: aggressive spatial downsampling, as some detection necks do

archetypes.name: dilated_3x3_d2_valid
archetypes.note: dilated and unpadded; the output shrinks by dilation * (R-1)

archetypes.name: downsample_2x2
archetypes.note: even filter at matching stride; a non-overlapping reduction

archetypes.name: mobilenet_depthwise_3x3
archetypes.note: depthwise: one filter per input channel, so groups == C == K

archetypes.name: grouped_3x3_c8
archetypes.note: an intermediate group count, as ShuffleNet-style blocks use

archetypes.name: video_3x3x3
archetypes.note: a 3-D (video) convolution stage: 3x3x3 filter, same padding, short clip depth

// archetypes: Correlated tuples from real networks (RFC 0019.13 §12.2). Realism is a joint fact: C=3 is a real convolution beside K=64, a 7x7 filter and a 224x224 image, and meaningless beside K=905. Each archetype fixes one coherent geometry -- filter size, dilation and padding together -- and varies stride inside it, because padding is chosen to suit the filter and dilation while stride is chosen independently of both. Between them these cover stride 1/2/4/16, padding 0 through 5, dilation 1 through 4, and group counts from 1 through depthwise.
// neighbourhood: How a draw may drift and stay a layer. R, S, stride, padding and dilation are all deliberately absent: they form one coupled geometry, and moving any of them alone breaks the pairing the archetypes exist to record -- a 7x7 that drifts to 3x3 while pad stays 3, or a 16x16 patch projection whose stride falls to 1, is valid and is in no network. Coverage of those axes comes from declaring more geometries, not from perturbing one. W repeats the 1 ratio because most images are square and a uniform draw over {1, 1.33, 2} would say otherwise.
// mixture: Anchors alone memorise a handful of shapes; the wide net alone put 0.04% of ten thousand draws anywhere near a real layer. The exploration share is §5.4's floor -- an engine still has to answer for problems nobody wrote down.
// spatial: spatial and layout are axes of the problem: 3-D problems add a depth to every tensor and to the geometry, and channels_last stores activations NHWC/NDHWC and the filter KRSC. 2-D problems pin every depth parameter to its identity.
